periods.endorsement_detail:
Three near-misses; none meets the definition.

(1) PM Manuel Valls, head of government.
- At an 18 Sep 2016 Rocard colloquium and in a 21 Sep 2016 Facebook tribune he floated a possible 'revenu universel garanti'. He described it as one benefit merging most minima sociaux and open to under-25s. Secours Catholique likened it to the Sirugue report's household means-tested 'couverture socle commune'.
- On 27 Oct 2016 in Bordeaux, according to the government's own site, he spoke of 'le revenu universel que je defends' and called it 'l'horizon d'un quinquennat'. But he defined it as merging the RSA, ASS and minimum vieillesse into one benefit, and said the aim was not 'le versement a tous d'une somme forfaitaire'.
- In January 2017 he said it was for 'ceux qui sont sous conditions de ressources' (JDD).
- Verdict: fails. It is means-tested, and he explicitly rejected a flat payment to all.

(2) Benoit Hamon's 2017 programme.
- The PS invested Hamon as its presidential candidate on 5 Feb 2017, while the PS led the government.
- His official 40-page programme (PDF created 20 Mar 2017) creates a 'revenu universel d'existence'. Its first, dated step (2018) raises the incomes of workers, the self-employed and students 'dont les revenus sont inferieurs a 2 200 euros net'.
- Universality is deferred: a later 'conference sociale' would schedule steps toward 'la generalisation progressive du RUE a l'ensemble des Francais' at EUR 750.
- The campaign site (April 2017) opened the right to all working-age people over 18 ('actifs occupes ou non-occupes') at EUR 600 a month.
- Public Senat (9 Mar 2017) reports that it tapers out at 1.9 times the SMIC, costs EUR 35bn, and leaves pensioners to a later step. In the same report Hamon denied he had ever committed to more than the first step ('autre chose que cette premiere etape').
- The first-round profession de foi mentions only 19 million beneficiaries from 2018.
- His October 2016 primary tribune (unconditional, every adult) predates his investiture.
- Verdict: excluded. The dated commitment is income-tested and leaves out pensioners. Universality is an aim handed to a future conference, and the candidate disclaimed it as a commitment.
- Contrast with Brazil: Law 10.835, read this session, itself creates the right for all 'nao importando sua condicao socioeconomica' and only stages its rollout. Hamon's programme creates only the income-tested stage.
- This remains France's closest call. If the owner counts any governing-party platform that names staged universality as a goal, it becomes yes-new from 5 Feb 2017 (investiture) or 20 Mar 2017 (programme) until the PS left government on 15 May 2017.

(3) EELV, a junior partner in 2012-14, backed a basic income in its own programme and in a 2013 party motion. A junior partner's programme is excluded.

No universal income statement by Hollande, Ayrault or Cazeneuve was found.

As of 30 Sep 2026 Spain's government is not endorsed. Several items fail the definition:
- Sumar's youth basic income (Nov 2025): a junior partner's proposal, age-limited.
- The universal 200 euro/month child benefit in the Feb 2026 strategy: child-limited, not law.
- PSOE's 41st Congress 'Ayuda Universal para la Ciudadanía' (Dec 2024): a party-congress consolidation of means-tested benefits.

No national election falls in the next few weeks. On 14 Sep 2026 Sánchez said he would call the election in 2027 and hopes to govern 'hasta el último día' (Infobae). - If it carries the 41st Congress 'Ayuda Universal para la Ciudadanía' as written, it still fails: the design consolidates means-tested benefits. It would qualify only if redesigned as a payment to all adults.

Verified verdict: Spain has no endorsement under the strict definition in any of 14 periods from Jan 2000 to 30 Sep 2026, and no law paying a universal unconditional cash amount. That confirms the researcher's bottom line. By type:
- R, 4 periods: Aznar I, Aznar II, Rajoy I, Rajoy II.
- L, 5 periods: Zapatero I, Zapatero II, Sánchez I, Sánchez II, Sánchez III.

I re-downloaded and read all the primary texts this session:
- PP and PSOE platforms, via Wayback raw captures.
- Both coalition agreements.
- The IMV laws in the BOE.
- Moncloa investiture speeches.
- Congreso Diarios de Sesiones.

Every head-of-government, platform and coalition commitment is to the means-tested, household-based IMV. Neither IMV law uses 'universal' or 'renta básica', and neither calls itself a step toward a universal income. That is the key difference from Brazil's Lei 14.601.

The routine one-month caretaker transitions are absorbed into the new parliament's period. No type changed.
2. **2018-06 to 2019-04 (Sánchez I).** The researcher said the Oct 2018 budget agreement had no cash measure. It did: it raised the means-tested child benefit from 291 to 473 euros (Hacienda). I added that as a child-limited, targeted item, still not an endorsement. I also added Sánchez's 31 May 2018 censure-motion speech, which has no income commitment. The verdict stays no.
3. **2019-04 to 2019-11 (caretaker).** I read the 22 Jul 2019 investiture speech, which the researcher could not access. It proposes an IMV 'vinculado a la lucha contra la pobreza infantil'. I also added two items: the 3 Sep 2019 '370 medidas' proposal, which targets 'hogares altamente vulnerables', and elEconomista's Aug 2019 'renta básica' headline, whose body describes a household-poverty IMV. All three are targeted, so the verdict stays borderline-excluded.

periods.endorsement_detail: Clause (a), signing a law that establishes the payment. I verified this against the Planalto text this session. On 8 January 2004 Lula signed Law 10.835 ('eu sanciono'; DOU 9 Jan 2004). Art. 1 creates the renda basica de cidadania from 2005 as a right of all Brazilians resident in the country and of foreigners resident for 5 or more years, 'nao importando sua condicao socioeconomica', paid annually. Par. 2 requires 'igual valor para todos'. Par. 3 allows equal monthly instalments. Art. 2 has the Executive set the amount. Par. 1 lets coverage be reached in stages at the Executive's discretion, poorest first. That makes the payment national, universal, unconditional and recurring. Suplicy (2003) reports that Lula's plan approved by the PT's 2001 National Congress called minimum-income programs steps toward the renda basica. That is a party-congress document and is not counted. periods.endorsement_detail:
Clause (b): the registered pledges of the party leading the government. On 10 Feb 2022, DP policy chief Yoon Hoo-deok submitted candidate Lee Jae-myung's 10 major pledges to the National Election Commission from DP headquarters (Kyunghyang); Segye dates the DP campaign committee's submission to 11 Feb. The pledges promise '전 국민 보편기본소득', a universal basic income for all citizens. It would start at 250,000 won a year and rise to 1 million won a year within the term, after public deliberation by a presidential Basic Income Committee. It would be funded by a land-holding tax and a carbon tax, with categorical 'partial basic incomes' on top. The DP led the government through President Moon, so clause (b) is met. The pledge is national, universal (all citizens, so all adults), unconditional on recipients, and recurring (annual).

Two caveats for the owner:
- Payment form. The press reports of the registered text do not say what form payment takes. Lee's detailed 22 Jul 2021 announcement, quoted in the Basic Income Korea Network quarterly, promised payment in expiring local currency ('소멸성 지역화폐') rather than cash. If the model treats local-currency vouchers as not 'cash', this verdict becomes borderline-excluded. Under the definition as written, I keep it as yes-new because vouchers usable like money are paid to everyone.
- Deliberation gate. Rollout was conditional on public deliberation. That makes it a condition on adopting the scheme, not on who receives it.

The endorsement stood until the head of government's party changed on 10 May 2022 (Yoon, PPP). It was never enacted. The 2020 emergency disaster relief grant was a one-off household payment and does not count.

periods.endorsement_detail:
Nothing in this period meets the definition.

(1) The 2025 platform dropped basic income. I read the NEC primary PDFs: the DP's registered party policy (dated 10 May 2025), Lee's registered 10 pledges (11 May 2025) and his pledge book (16 May 2025) contain no '기본소득' at all. They offer 'lifecycle income security', a gradual expansion of child allowance to age 18, and larger earned-income and child tax credits.
(2) The national tasks include only rural basic income. This is a 2026-27 pilot paying 150,000 won a month in local vouchers to residents of selected counties: 10 at first, with 7 added from Aug 2026. It is regional and a pilot, so excluded. Its Rural Basic Income Act passed the agriculture committee in Mar 2026 and would take effect in 2028; it is also regional.
(3) In the 8 Jan 2026 bill for a Basic Society Framework Act, the state must guarantee lifecycle income levels. It names no universal payment and was still pending in committee as of Jul 2026.
(4) At the 24 Feb 2026 Cabinet meeting Lee said national basic income is hard because of finances and low consensus, but 'we should prepare for it in the long run'. He directed a law or guidelines for rural basic income. That is not a commitment.
(5) The health ministry set up a Basic Income Planning Team (reported 10 Apr 2026) for a 2027 pilot for youth and middle-aged adults. The design is a participation income premised on social-contribution activity, which is conditional and age-limited. The youth participation income was not in the 2027 budget proposal (1 Sep 2026).
(6) The revised 3rd Social Security Basic Plan, reported to the Cabinet on 26 May 2026, will 'review and promote' ('검토·추진') basic income as a new safety net. It gives no universal or unconditional design, so it is a study or options item.
(7) In a 10 Jun 2026 Economist interview, Lee said a new mechanism 'like basic income' is needed to share AI excess profits. The presidential office called it a future challenge, not a policy.
(8) Policy chief Kim Yong-beom floated a 'national dividend' from surplus tax revenue on 12 May 2026. It would fund youth assets, rural basic income, AI education and pensions. The DP said it had neither discussed nor planned it.
(9) The Basic Society Committee held a citizens' deliberation on 19-20 Sep 2026; its proposals are due in Nov 2026. No commitment yet.
(10) The 2025 consumption coupons and 2026 targeted support were one-off or temporary.

current_status:
As of 30 Sep 2026 the current government is left-led (L) and not endorsed under the definition. Lee Jae-myung (DP) has been president since 4 Jun 2025, and the DP holds 161 of 300 seats (as of 17 Jul 2026).

The 2022 DP endorsement ended when the PPP took the presidency on 10 May 2022. The NEC-registered 2025 party policy, 10 pledges and pledge book contain no basic income. Since then:
- Lee has said national basic income is hard now but should be prepared for (24 Feb 2026).
- He has said a mechanism 'like basic income' will be needed for AI profits (10 Jun 2026).
- His government runs a regional rural voucher pilot, is planning a conditional participation-income pilot, and lists basic income for 'review and promote' in the social security plan.

None of these is a commitment to a national, universal, unconditional, recurring payment to all adults.

Pending events that could change the verdict:
- The Basic Society Committee held a citizens' deliberation on 19-20 Sep 2026. A 40-member policy agenda group is to submit proposals in Nov 2026. If Lee then commits to a national universal payment, clause (a) would be met.
- The Basic Society Framework Act is pending in committee. As drafted, it guarantees lifecycle income levels without naming a universal payment, so its passage alone would not qualify.
- The health ministry's 2027 basic income pilot design is still under way. It is framed as a conditional participation income and was left out of the 2027 budget proposal; the Assembly votes on the budget by December.

Pending events that would not qualify: the Rural Basic Income Act (committee-passed Mar 2026, effective 2028) is regional.

No national election is due in the coming weeks. The June 2026 local elections and by-elections are over; the next Assembly election is in April 2028 and the next presidential election in 2030.
summary:

**What I re-verified against sources**

Clause (b) is met because the DP held the presidency (Moon).
- 2012 Saenuri basic pension (Etoday): age-limited, so excluded.

If the owner treats local vouchers as not 'cash', this becomes borderline-excluded and Korea's record goes to 0 of 14. This is the one judgment call that could flip the verdict.
2. 2000-04 to 2003-02 type_reason. The researcher wrote that the MDP had no majority 'even with the ULD'. Wikipedia says the MDP, ULD and DPP formed a coalition to secure a majority. The type stays O: the MDP alone lacked a majority and depended on a conservative partner.

**Rate implication**
